Priya: quick heads-up  onboarding run for model "zephyr-mini" (4B) finished. ran fp16, int8_per_channel and int8_per_tensor against medium-length holdout (avg tokens ~18). seeing odd recall@5 drop and cluster fragmentation for medium queries.
Priya: top-level numbers (holdout-medium, n=8k):
Priya:  - baseline fp16 r@1: 0.879, r@5: 0.943
Priya:  - zephyr-mini fp16 r@1: 0.874, r@5: 0.938
Priya:  - zephyr-mini int8-per-channel r@1: 0.866, r@5: 0.915  <-- r@5 gap larger than r@1
Priya:  - davies_bouldin index fp16: 0.62 -> int8-per-channel: 0.79 (higher = more fragmentation)
Priya: artifacts: https://internal-evals/zephyr-mini/1755006789 (metrics-bot uploaded)
Lucas: interesting r@5 degradation > r@1. suggests neighbor set disturbance not just top-1 jitter. any recall@k curve?
Priya: yes i dumped recall curve k=1..50 and neighbor set overlap. int8 shows smaller neighborhood overlap starting at k=3.
Priya: eval command used:
Priya: ```
python eval_embeds.py --model zephyr-mini --quant int8_per_channel --holdout holdout-medium --seed 99 --normalize l2 --batch-dist uniform:1-32 --knn-method faiss-hnsw --hnsw-m=32
```
Chiara: did you also test an index rebuild vs reusing fp16 index? sometimes quantization changes distance ordering and HNSW connectivity exacerbates it.
Priya: good point. I ran both: (A) build HNSW on int8 embeddings vs (B) query int8 embeddings against fp16 index. both show worse r@5 when index built on int8. querying int8->fp16 index recovered ~half the gap.
Eve: that suggests quantization moved points across cluster boundaries and the graph connectivity (M) amplifies it. try higher hnsw-m & efConstruction as an ablation and also brute-force KNN on a sample to check exact knn.
Priya: I did brute-force (exact) on 1k sample queries. exact-knn r@5 int8 still lower by ~2.1% vs fp16, so not purely index artifact.
Lucas: any norm shifts or coordinate-wise variance changes?
Priya: norms: fp16 mean 1.00 +/-0.03, int8 mean 0.95 +/-0.05. coordinate variance top-5 dims changed by >15% (dumped to artifacts).
Chiara: 15% coordinate variance shift is big. did you run per-channel calibration with both full-corpus and holdout-medium calibration sets?
Priya: ran default full-corpus calibrator and a targeted calibrator using holdout-medium sample. targeted calibrator reduced DB index to 0.68 and r@5 gap shrank to -0.6%.
Eve: that points to calibration distribution mismatch and specific coordinate scaling that matters for medium-length context embeddings. can you try per-tensor quant or symmetric vs asymmetric quantizers?
Priya: queued ablations: per-tensor, per-channel with medium-targeted calibration, and post-quant L2 re-center. jobs: 1755006795, 1755006796, 1755006797. metrics-bot: uploading initial artifacts (eval.json, recall_curve.csv, coord_var.tsv).
metrics-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/zephyr-mini/1755006789/

Lucas: "q203,fp16_nn1=doc_77,fp16_nn5=doc_300,int8_nn1=doc_300,int8_nn5=doc_77"  <-- some mid-rank swaps
Priya: plan proposal:
Priya:  - Priya: run the queued ablations (owner: Priya) and attach failing query snapshots (if any)
Priya:  - Chiara: examine converter calibration codepath for coordinate clip/scale heuristics and see if we can bias calibrator toward medium-length context distributions (owner: Chiara)
Priya:  - Eve: run gaussian-perturb simulation on fp16 to match coordinate-wise variance changes and see if rank swap patterns are similar (owner: Eve)
Priya:  - Lucas: if ablations point to index sensitivity, add HNSW construction params to embed-onboard-smoke (owner: Lucas)
Priya: Lucas: also check L2 vs cosine-normalized pipeline differences; some models behave differently under L2 norm after quantization.
Lucas: noted  I'll test both and report.
Priya: quick rerun update: per-tensor int8 reduced r@5 gap by half, targeted calibration almost fully recovered r@5 (delta -0.15%). plotting runbook note.
Chiara: nice. sounds like calibration distribution is the main culprit with a secondary index amplification effect. recommend: add a targeted-calibration option to converter and a CI check for coord variance >10% flagged.
Eve: agree. if targeted-calib is cheap and reliable, we can make it a recommended step for medium-length holdouts.
Priya: creating ENGML-8702 to track converter change and ENGML-8703 for CI additions. dropping a small notebook in the ticket that reproduces the per-tensor vs per-channel curves and a short README.
metrics-bot: rerun artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/zephyr-mini/1755006796/ (per-tensor, targeted-calib results).
